toc.title: Model choice, inference parameters, RAG and vector stores

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation; AI: artificial intelligence; ETL: extract, transform, load; IAM: Identity and Access Management; KMS: Key Management Service; VPC: Virtual Private Cloud; SDK: software development kit; FM: foundation model

  • Identify the criteria for choosing a foundation model, including prompt caching
  • Describe how inference parameters such as temperature change responses
  • Define RAG, name its business uses and the vector stores on AWS
  • Explain the cost trade-offs of customization approaches
  • Define the role of AI agents and their business uses

2Model choice, inference parameters, RAG and vector stores

Running case

Cedar and Salt Designs the Booking Assistant

  • Cedar and Salt will build a booking assistant that answers policy questions and plans trips
  • Engineers ask: which model, which settings, and how do we use our own documents?
  • They also ask: where do we store embeddings, do we tune the model, and can it act for guests?
  • Your job: make the design choices the exam names

Criteria for Choosing a Foundation Model

Criterion Ask
Cost What is the price per input and output token?
Modality Text, image, audio or video, in and out?
Latency How fast must the answer arrive?
Multi-lingual Does it work well in our guests' languages?
Model size Bigger is more capable, but costs more
Model complexity Is a simpler model enough?
Customization Can we tune or distill it?
Input and output length Do our documents fit the context window?
Prompt caching Is it supported, to cut repeated cost?
Exam tip

Match the need to the criterion: speed is latency, many languages is multi-lingual, long documents is input length.

Reading the Criteria

  • Size and complexity: a larger model is usually slower and costlier; start with the smallest that meets the quality bar
  • Input and output length: the context window caps what goes in; output length caps the answer; more tokens mean more cost and time
  • Multi-lingual: test quality in each language you serve, not only English
  • Customization: some models can be fine-tuned or distilled; check this before you choose
  • Modality: a task that reads photos needs a multi-modal model
Exam tip

Documents too long for the model: pick a longer context window, or retrieve only the relevant parts.

Prompt Caching [Verify live]

  • Prompt caching is an optional feature that cuts response latency and input token cost
  • Best for long, repeated context: many questions about one uploaded document
  • Implicit caching is automatic; explicit caching uses cache checkpoints you set
  • Put static content first and changing content last, so the prefix can match
  • The cache has a time to live, often 5 minutes, reset by each hit
  • Cache writes, reads and normal tokens are billed at different rates; a hit is not guaranteed
  • Not for batch inference
  • As of 5 November 2026: support, minimum size and time to live vary by model
Exam tip

The same long context sent again and again: prompt caching.

Inference Parameters: Temperature, Top K and Top P

Parameter Lower value Higher value
Temperature More predictable: likelier tokens win More varied: unlikely tokens get a chance
Top K Fewer candidate tokens (a fixed number) More candidate tokens
Top P A smaller share of probability; pool size varies A larger share of probability
  • Candidates: horses 0.7, zebras 0.2, unicorns 0.1. Top K of 2 keeps horses and zebras; Top P of 0.7 keeps only horses
  • Defaults and ranges depend on the model
Exam tip

Factual and consistent: low temperature. Creative and varied: high temperature.

Length Parameters and Stop Sequences

  • Response length: the maximum (or minimum) number of tokens to return
  • A limit that is too low cuts the answer off; higher allows long answers but costs more and takes longer
  • Stop sequences: text that stops generation as soon as the model writes it
  • Penalties: discourage repeated or frequent tokens, or very long responses
  • Input length: the prompt, documents and history must fit the context window
  • Under on-demand pricing you pay for tokens in and tokens out
Exam tip

An answer that stops mid-sentence: raise the maximum response length.

Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)

  • RAG draws information from your own data store to augment what the model answers
  • It needs no retraining, keeps answers current and can cite sources
  • Grounding in real documents helps reduce hallucinations

Exam tip

Use our own, current documents without retraining: RAG.

Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases

  • Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases is managed RAG: an out-of-the-box solution that automates the pipeline
  • Ingestion: connect a data source such as documents in Amazon S3; text is split into chunks, turned into embeddings and stored in a vector index
  • At question time: embed the question, search the index, add the chunks to the prompt, then generate the answer
  • Returns direct quotations from sources or a natural response
  • No need to keep training the model on your private data
  • Quick create can build a vector store for you, or you can bring your own
Exam tip

Managed RAG on AWS: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases.

Business Applications of RAG

  • Customer support: a chat that answers from policy and help pages
  • Internal knowledge search: staff ask about procedures and policies
  • Document question answering: answers from contracts and reports, with citations
  • Personalization: recommendations that use customer and product data
  • Research: find and summarize facts across many long documents
Exam tip

Private or fast-changing knowledge behind an answer: RAG.

Vector Databases: AWS Services That Store Embeddings

Service Role as a vector store
Amazon OpenSearch Service Distributed search and analytics; full-text plus vector search
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Relational database with the pgvector extension
Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) for PostgreSQL Managed PostgreSQL with pgvector
Amazon Neptune Analytics Graph analytics with vector search, for GraphRAG
Amazon DocumentDB Document database with native vector search
Amazon MemoryDB In-memory, ultra-low latency vector search
Amazon S3 Vectors Low-cost vector storage for infrequent queries
  • ElastiCache for Valkey also offers vector search, and DynamoDB data can be searched by vector through a zero-ETL link to OpenSearch Service
Exam tip

Know the four named in the guide: OpenSearch Service, Aurora, Neptune and RDS for PostgreSQL.

Choosing a Vector Store

If you need Choose
Structured query language (SQL) and vector queries in one database Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector
High-throughput search, with full-text OpenSearch Service
Relationships between entities (GraphRAG) Neptune Analytics
Billions of vectors at the lowest cost S3 Vectors
A MongoDB-compatible application DocumentDB
No infrastructure to manage Knowledge Bases with quick create
  • All of these work with IAM, KMS encryption and VPC support
  • The embeddings model's dimensions must match the vector index
Exam tip

Existing PostgreSQL: pgvector. Graph relationships: Neptune. Full-text plus vector: OpenSearch.

3Customization costs, agents and practice

Customizing a Model: The Cost Ladder

  • Prompts and in-context learning: no training; you pay for the tokens in longer prompts
  • RAG: no training; adds embeddings, a vector store and retrieval, plus longer prompts
  • Fine-tuning or continued pre-training: training is billed on tokens processed times epochs, plus monthly storage
  • Distillation: pay to train once, then run a smaller, faster, cheaper model
  • Pre-training: typically the highest resources and cost

Exam tip

Cheapest first: prompts, then RAG, then tuning, then building a model.

Which Approach, and When?

Situation Approach
The task works, but wording needs help Prompt engineering, with examples in the prompt
Answers need current or private facts RAG
A specific task and labeled data Fine-tuning
Domain-specific language, such as legal terms Continued pre-training or fine-tuning
A big model is too slow or costly for a narrow task Distillation to a smaller model
No model fits and you hold vast data Pre-train a custom model
  • The Well-Architected Generative AI Lens: start with the least resource-intensive option, and evaluate after each step
Exam tip

Do not customize first; prompts and RAG come before tuning.

AI Agents Old name [Verify live]

  • An AI agent uses a foundation model to understand a request and break it into smaller steps
  • It calls APIs of company systems, asks the user for missing details and queries knowledge bases to add information
  • Agents for Amazon Bedrock orchestrate models, data sources, applications and conversations
  • That service is now Amazon Bedrock Agents Classic; for new agents, AWS points to the Strands Agents SDK and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
  • As of 5 November 2026: new sign-ups for Agents Classic are closed; existing users continue
Exam tip

A multi-step task that calls APIs is an agent; the exam may still say Agents for Amazon Bedrock.

Business Applications of AI Agents

  • Insurance claims: the agent gathers details, checks the policy and files the claim
  • Travel reservations: the agent finds options, asks for missing details and books through an API
  • Customer service: answers questions and takes actions, such as changing a booking
  • Task automation: repeats routine steps across company systems
  • Agent versus RAG: RAG answers from documents; an agent also acts
Exam tip

Answers a question from documents: RAG. Completes a multi-step task through APIs: an agent.

What the Exam Asks: Designing with FMs

  • Which criterion: cost, modality, latency, languages, size, complexity, customization, length or caching
  • Which parameter: temperature, Top K, Top P, response length or stop sequence
  • Which approach: prompts first, RAG for current data, fine-tuning for a specific task
  • Which store: OpenSearch Service, Aurora, RDS for PostgreSQL, Neptune and others
  • Which feature: Knowledge Bases for managed RAG, agents for multi-step tasks
Exam tip

Name the need first, then the criterion, setting, approach or service.

Design Check: Cedar and Salt's Assistant

Cedar and Salt needs Choose
Answers in about a second on a tight budget A smaller model; check latency and price per token
Guests write in several languages A multi-lingual model, tested in each
The same long policy goes with every question Prompt caching
Policy answers must be consistent A low temperature
Policies change every week RAG with Knowledge Bases
Link hotels, partners and trips by relationships Neptune Analytics (GraphRAG)
Find options, ask details and book a trip An agent
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1A developer lowers the temperature of a foundation model from a high value to a low value. What is the most likely effect?

  • AResponses become more varied and more creative
  • BResponses become more consistent and predictable
  • CResponses become cut off after a fixed length
  • DResponses become longer and more detailed
Show the answer

Answer: B. A lower temperature steepens the probability distribution, so the model picks higher-probability tokens and responds more deterministically. A higher temperature gives more random, varied responses. Length is set with response length parameters.

S2Cedar and Salt's assistant sends the same long policy document with every guest question, and cost and latency are high. Which feature helps most?

  • APrompt caching for the repeated policy text
  • BA higher temperature to speed up the answers
  • CA larger Top K value to lower the token price
  • DA longer stop sequence to shorten the prompt
Show the answer

Answer: A. Prompt caching reuses a repeated prompt prefix, which reduces latency and input token cost for long, repeated context. Temperature, Top K and stop sequences do not change how a repeated prompt is processed or billed.

S3Which TWO are criteria for choosing a foundation model for an application? (Select TWO.)

  • AThe brand colors of the model provider
  • BThe latency and the price per token
  • CThe number of staff on the support team
  • DThe input and output length limits
  • EThe office location of the model developers
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. Latency, price per token and input and output length are selection criteria, together with modality, languages, size, complexity, customization and prompt caching. Branding, staffing and office location do not describe the model.

S4Cedar and Salt's cancellation policy changes every week, and the assistant must use the latest text without retraining. Which approach fits best?

  • APre-train a new foundation model each week on the policy
  • BFine-tune the model each week with the new policy text
  • CRaise the temperature so the model infers new policies
  • DUse RAG with a knowledge base synced to the policy files
Show the answer

Answer: D. RAG retrieves current documents at question time, so updating the data source is enough, and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases manages the pipeline. Pre-training and fine-tuning cost time and money every time, and temperature adds no facts.

S5Cedar and Salt wants answers that follow relationships between hotels, partners and trips, using vector search with graph traversal. Which service fits?

  • AAmazon S3 Vectors, for the lowest-cost vector storage
  • BAmazon Neptune Analytics, for GraphRAG with vector search
  • CAmazon MemoryDB, for in-memory vector search at low latency
  • DAmazon DocumentDB, for MongoDB-compatible vector search
Show the answer

Answer: B. Neptune Analytics combines vector search with graph traversals and algorithms, which suits GraphRAG. S3 Vectors suits cheap, infrequent retrieval, MemoryDB suits ultra-low latency, and DocumentDB suits MongoDB-compatible applications.

S6Which approach to improving a model's answers usually costs the least and should be tried first?

  • APre-training a new foundation model from scratch
  • BContinued pre-training on large domain datasets
  • CPrompt engineering with examples in the prompt
  • DDistillation from a large teacher into a small model
Show the answer

Answer: C. The Well-Architected Generative AI Lens says to start with the least resource-intensive option, prompt engineering, then evaluate RAG, and customize only if needed. Building a custom model is typically the highest in resources and cost.

S7Which TWO statements describe what an AI agent does? (Select TWO.)

  • AIt breaks a request into smaller steps and calls APIs to carry them out
  • BIt removes the need for any foundation model in the application
  • CIt stores the model weights and the training data in Amazon S3
  • DIt guarantees that every action it takes is correct
  • EIt can query a knowledge base to add information while it works
Show the answer

Answer: A, E. An agent uses a foundation model to understand a request, break it into steps, take actions through API calls and query data sources or knowledge bases. It still needs a model, it does not store weights, and it cannot guarantee correctness.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Model criteria cost, modality, latency, languages, size, complexity, customization, length and prompt caching
Parameters a low temperature gives steady answers; Top K and Top P limit candidates; length settings cap the output
RAG adds your own, current data without retraining; Knowledge Bases is managed RAG
Vector stores OpenSearch Service, Aurora, RDS for PostgreSQL, Neptune and more
Customization cost prompts, then RAG, then tuning or distillation, then pre-training
Agents break tasks into steps and call APIs
